orientation.title: Before you code
orientation.description: Get a quick idea of what software developers actually do and how software is built.
orientation.starter_activity: Think of a simple problem you face every day. Write down the steps you would want a computer to follow to solve it.

goal: Build a small web application and discover whether you enjoy solving problems through code.
tasks: Learn the basics of HTML and CSS
Build a simple webpage
Add basic JavaScript functionality
Write a small Python program
Combine your ideas into a mini project
Test and improve your project
Reflect on whether you enjoyed the process

orientation.title: Before you analyze
orientation.description: Understand what data analysts do and how raw information can become useful insights.
orientation.starter_activity: Look around your daily life and identify three things that could be measured as data—for example, study time, expenses or screen time.

goal: Use a small dataset to discover and communicate useful insights.
tasks: Choose a small public dataset
Explore the data
Clean the data
Find three interesting patterns
Create three visualizations
Write a short insight report
Reflect on whether you enjoyed the process

orientation.title: Before you design
orientation.description: Learn the difference between UI and UX and understand how designers solve problems for real users.
orientation.starter_activity: Choose an app or website you use every day. Write down one thing that is easy to use and one thing that could be improved.

goal: Design a simple digital product from a real user problem.
tasks: Identify a user problem
Research potential users
Sketch three possible solutions
Create a simple wireframe
Design the main interface
Ask someone to test your design
Reflect on what you learned

orientation.title: Before you make an impact
orientation.description: Understand how social impact work identifies community problems and develops practical solutions.
orientation.starter_activity: Think of one problem in your school, college or community. Write down who is affected and one possible way to help.

goal: Explore a real community problem and design a small, practical solution.
tasks: Choose a community problem you care about
Research who is affected by the problem
Identify the main causes of the problem
Explore existing solutions
Design a small practical solution
Explain your solution to someone and gather feedback
Reflect on whether you enjoyed the process

orientation.title: Before you market
orientation.description: Understand how digital marketers use content, research and online platforms to reach and engage audiences.
orientation.starter_activity: Choose a brand or organization you know. Look at one of its social media posts and write down who you think it is trying to reach and what action it wants people to take.

goal: Plan and test a simple digital marketing campaign for a real or imaginary organization.
tasks: Choose a brand, organization or imaginary product
Identify its target audience
Research what the audience cares about
Create a simple marketing message
Design a social media post or campaign idea
Review your campaign and explain why it could work
Reflect on whether you enjoyed the process

orientation.title: Before you create
orientation.description: Explore how content creators turn ideas into written, visual and multimedia stories for different audiences.
orientation.starter_activity: Choose a topic you care about and imagine you need to explain it to someone who knows nothing about it. Write down three different ways you could present the idea.

goal: Create a small piece of audience-focused content and discover whether you enjoy the creative process.
tasks: Choose a topic and identify your target audience
Research the topic and collect useful information
Write a short piece of content
Create a simple visual to support your message
Combine your writing and visual into one content piece
Share your work with someone and gather feedback
Reflect on whether you enjoyed the process
